alignments.note: The participle's subject is expressed by the substantival article οἱ, so under rule 74's expressed-subject arm the participle keeps only the supplied subordinator and its own verb; discontinuous under rule 15. This is the same construction MAT.20.10 (ἐλθόντες οἱ πρῶτοι) and MAT.20.24 (ἀκούσαντες οἱ δέκα) read the same way, which is rule 24's habit.

Substantival article whose modifier is a prepositional phrase: it takes the discontinuous *they … that* whole, rule 32's stated contrast (`οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ` → *they … that are with him*) and rule 31's clause that a substantival article takes the supplied nominal along with the relativizer. Head on the nominal word and never on the relativizer, rule 22. The subject word *they* is not a supplied helper on the participle, the Greek having expressed the subject in this article.

The prepositional phrase is the predicate, so the supplied lexical verb rides with the preposition and the head stands on the prepositional word, rule 62; rule 11 keeps the italics from making *were hired* added.
Distributive ἀνά rendered *every man*; head on *every* rather than on the supplied generic noun, rule 17.
Anarthrous noun with supplied indefinite determiner, rule 51's anarthrous clause.

review_notes: Corrected: the accepted alignment treated *they* as a supplied subject on ἐλθόντες under rule 74, but rule 74's supplied-subject arm reaches only a participial clause whose subject the Greek leaves unexpressed. Here the substantival article οἱ expresses it, so the subject word is that token's own aligned English and the participle keeps only *when … came*.

The article accordingly carries the discontinuous *they … that*, rule 32's contrast for an article whose modifier is a prepositional phrase with no verb to carry a relativizer, headed on *they* under rule 22.
This also brings the verse into line with MAT.20.10 and MAT.20.24, where the same participle-plus-expressed-subject frame leaves the participle only its subordinator and verb.
